messages.author: 71bfb5f1e96782a8
messages.subject: SRMR in cfa with ordered variables
parts:
Hello once again,

i fit a cfa-model with the cfa function and the "WLMSV" estimator. When i look into the summary(model, fit.measures = TRUE) i find CLI, TFI, RMSEA, chi-sq, but not the SRMR. Why is that?

Best, Hans

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: SRMR in cfa with ordered variables
parts:
On 11/23/2012 04:01 PM, Dr. Hans Hansen wrote:
> Hello once again,
>
> i fit a cfa-model with the cfa function and the "WLMSV" estimator. When
> i look into the summary(model, fit.measures = TRUE) i find CLI, TFI,
> RMSEA, chi-sq, but not the SRMR. Why is that?

Because it is not clear how to compute the SRMR in the presence of
thresholds. If there would be no meanstructure (no thresholds), it
should be possible to compute it.

But if you could point to relevant literature about this saying
otherwise, I would happy to adjust the current behavior.

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: SRMR in cfa with ordered variables
parts:
On 06/27/2018 11:00 AM, Felix Fischer wrote:
> Hi Yves,
>
> i am wondering about this as well - can you give some recommendations
> whether one should use the SRMR in CFAs for categorial data and what
> threshold makes sense?

I am not aware of any literature (but I may have missed it!). It just
makes sense to me (and many others, who suggested it to me). In the
categorical case, both the implied/observed 'covariance' matrices are in
fact correlation matrices. So the SRMR, in a way, gives you the
'average' difference between those correlations. In a metric that is
simple to understand: the correlation metric. You can use your own
cut-off value, depending on what -in your field- would be considered a
large/medium/small difference between two correlations.

Yves.
